metadata.name: Blank Project Guide
metadata.description: A guided starting point for any project type. This template provides structure and helpful instructions to guide you through creating your plan from scratch. Perfect for unique projects, custom workflows, or learning how to use the plan builder.
metadata.author: Copilot Orchestration Extension

project.name: Project Name
project.description: 📝 GUIDE: Describe your project in 2-3 sentences. What are you building? Who will use it? What problem does it solve?
project.vision: 📝 GUIDE: What is the long-term vision? Where do you want this project to be in 1 year?
goals: 📝 GUIDE: Goal 1 - What measurable outcome do you want to achieve?
📝 GUIDE: Goal 2 - Success metric or KPI

architecture.pattern: 📝 GUIDE: Choose a pattern (Layered, Microservices, Monolithic, Event-Driven, etc.) or describe your own
architecture.description: 📝 GUIDE: Explain how the system is organized. What are the main layers or components?
components: 📝 GUIDE: Component 1 - What is it and what does it do?
📝 GUIDE: Component 2 - How does it interact with other components?
📝 GUIDE: Add more components as needed
architecture.rationale: 📝 GUIDE: Why did you choose this architecture? What are the benefits and trade-offs?

technology_stack.frontend: 📝 GUIDE: e.g., React, Vue, Angular, or None if backend-only
technology_stack.backend: 📝 GUIDE: e.g., Node.js, Python, Go, Java
technology_stack.infrastructure: 📝 GUIDE: e.g., Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, Azure

features.name: 📝 GUIDE: Core Feature Title
features.description: 📝 GUIDE: What does this feature do? Why is it important? Example: 'User authentication with email and password'
acceptance_criteria: 📝 GUIDE: What must be true for this feature to be considered complete?
📝 GUIDE: How will you know it works? (testable criteria)
features.notes: 📝 GUIDE: Any special considerations or implementation hints

features.name: 📝 GUIDE: Add More Features
features.description: 📝 GUIDE: Repeat this structure for each feature. Start with high-level features first, then break them down later.

phases.name: 📝 GUIDE: Phase 1 - Planning & Design
phases.description: 📝 GUIDE: What should happen in this phase? (e.g., Requirements gathering, architecture design, setup)

phases.name: 📝 GUIDE: Phase 2 - Development
phases.description: 📝 GUIDE: Main development phase. Can be broken into multiple sprints or milestones.

phases.name: 📝 GUIDE: Phase 3 - Testing & Launch
phases.description: 📝 GUIDE: Testing, bug fixes, performance optimization, and launch preparation

milestones.name: 📝 GUIDE: Milestone 1 - MVP Ready
milestones.description: 📝 GUIDE: What defines a successful milestone? (e.g., all core features working)

milestones.name: 📝 GUIDE: Milestone 2 - Production Ready
milestones.description: 📝 GUIDE: Final readiness check before launch

members.role_name: 📝 GUIDE: Your Role (e.g., Full Stack Developer)
responsibilities: 📝 GUIDE: What are your main responsibilities?
📝 GUIDE: What tasks will you own?
members.agent_mapping: 📝 GUIDE: Which AI agent(s) can help? (Auto Zen, Testing Agent, etc.)

team.structure: 📝 GUIDE: Agile, Waterfall, Kanban, or Hybrid?
team.communication_plan: 📝 GUIDE: How will team members communicate? (Daily standups, Weekly reviews, Slack channel, etc.)

success_criteria: 📝 GUIDE: Criterion 1 - What does success look like? (must be measurable)
📝 GUIDE: Criterion 2 - How will you know the project is successful?
📝 GUIDE: Criterion 3 - Add more criteria as needed

risks.description: 📝 GUIDE: What could go wrong? (e.g., Technical complexity, resource constraints, scope creep)
risks.mitigation: 📝 GUIDE: What's your plan to prevent or handle this risk?
risks.contingency: 📝 GUIDE: What's your backup plan if this happens?

risks.description: 📝 GUIDE: Add more risks as you identify them during planning
risks.mitigation: The more risks you identify upfront, the better prepared you are

assumptions: 📝 GUIDE: Assumption 1 - What are you assuming to be true? (e.g., Budget will be available)
📝 GUIDE: Assumption 2 - Team members are available full-time
📝 GUIDE: Assumption 3 - List all assumptions about resources, timeline, scope, etc.
constraints: 📝 GUIDE: Constraint 1 - What limitations do you have? (budget, timeline, resources, technical)
📝 GUIDE: Constraint 2 - Must be completed by deadline
📝 GUIDE: Constraint 3 - List all constraints that could impact the project

dependencies.description: 📝 GUIDE: External or internal dependency (e.g., another project must complete first)

quality_assurance.testing_strategy: 📝 GUIDE: How will you ensure quality? (unit tests, integration tests, E2E tests, manual testing)
browsers_supported: 📝 GUIDE: e.g., Chrome, Firefox, Safari (if web app)

environments.name: Staging
environments.deployment_method: 📝 GUIDE: e.g., Docker, Kubernetes, AWS ECS

environments.name: Production
environments.description: 📝 GUIDE: Live environment for end users
environments.deployment_method: 📝 GUIDE: How will you deploy to production?

deployment_strategy.rollback_plan: 📝 GUIDE: How will you handle failed deployments or bugs in production?
deployment_strategy.monitoring: 📝 GUIDE: How will you monitor the application? (Sentry, New Relic, CloudWatch, etc.)

documentation.user_docs: 📝 GUIDE: Will you create user guides or help documentation?
documentation.api_docs: 📝 GUIDE: If building an API, how will it be documented? (OpenAPI/Swagger, etc.)
documentation.architecture_docs: 📝 GUIDE: Document your system design for future developers
documentation.contributing_guide: 📝 GUIDE: If open source, how can others contribute?

optionalCustomizations.guidance: Clear goals help you stay focused and measure success
Start with high-level features, then break them down into smaller tasks
Realistic timelines help with resource planning
Clear role assignment prevents confusion and overlap
Proactive risk management helps avoid problems later

tips: 💡 Start with the 'project' section - describe WHAT you're building and WHY
💡 Use the 'architecture' section to describe HOW you'll build it
💡 List features in priority order - critical first, nice-to-have last
💡 Be realistic with effort estimates - 1 feature = 6-40 hours typically
💡 Identify risks early - the more you anticipate, the better prepared you are
💡 Define success criteria BEFORE you start building - how will you know when you're done?
💡 Use the AI Assistant (💡 button) to get suggestions for your plan
💡 Once satisfied, the Plan Decomposition Engine will break this into executable tasks
nextSteps: 1. Fill in the project name and description
2. Choose an architecture pattern or describe your own
3. List your main features in priority order
6. Click 'Complete Plan' to decompose into tasks
7. Review generated tasks and adjust as needed

guidance.onboarding: 🎓 This is a guided template! Each section has 📝 GUIDE comments showing what to fill in. Delete the guide text and replace with your project details.

sections_overview.project: Define WHAT you're building - name, description, vision, and goals
sections_overview.architecture: Describe HOW you'll build it - pattern, components, and technology stack
sections_overview.features: List the features you need to build, with acceptance criteria for each
sections_overview.timeline: Break project into phases and milestones with realistic dates
sections_overview.team: Define roles, responsibilities, and who owns what
sections_overview.quality_assurance: How will you ensure the project meets quality standards?
sections_overview.deployment: Where and how will you deploy this project?
sections_overview.risks: What could go wrong? How will you handle it?
sections_overview.success_criteria: How will you measure if the project was successful?

quick_start.step1: Replace 'Project Name' with your actual project name
quick_start.step2: Write a 2-3 sentence description of what you're building
quick_start.step3: List 3-5 main features you want to build
quick_start.step4: Estimate how long this will take (days, weeks, months)
quick_start.step5: Click 'Complete Plan' to decompose into tasks
